summary: w211 plan written as far as it goes (plan.md, parts 1-5). Taken: Retires are the @r1/@r3 @deprecated titles (the parenthesised r44/r45 name what they were deprecated for); sides from the repository's relation to the request, internal requests keep one repository (r33 rows 3-4, r34); repository identity from spec/index.md for r32; refusal order empty delegation, missing file, strict form, asker, origin, neither-flag; work show <request> per r25/r13; take-in is a work subcommand that work run calls before intake rounds (r39-r43, r40, decision 0071); a zero-line lines file stays as it is (no accepted requirement touches it). Live single-repository scenarios (r19, r22, r2, work-queue r7, the turn/outcome ones) stay green by binding their shared Givens to an internal request of ctx-a, so the work-queue r7 conflict needs no ruling. Two questions remain: the carrier of what is sent (and what each side sees before take-in), and whether r28 binds supervision's raise (r135).
questions: Carrier of what an asker sends (requests r28, r39-r44, decision 0071): r28/r44/r29 say the upstream keeps the request right after the asker's work request, with no checkout of the upstream; r39/r41 say it is kept only once taken in; r28 rows 2-3 and r33 row 1 have the asker answer a question only the upstream wrote. Reading A (git transport): the asker pushes each request or message to a ref namespace named by its asker id on the upstream's remote and fetches the upstream's requests to read questions; the narrator configures the upstream's remote, the upstream's work list shows nothing until take-in, and the namespace is the registration. Reading B (drop directory): a shared directory set in each repository's settings, one subdirectory per registered asker id, and the asker keeps its own copy of each request it raised; the narrator configures a drop path, the upstream sees nothing until take-in, and the asker sees questions only from what the upstream writes back to the drop.

Does requests r28 bind supervision's raise (supervision r135)? Reading A (no): work run keeps writing a raised request straight into the upstream's checkout, and the r30-r32 checks run only in the work request command; supervision's narrator sees no change, and features/supervision.feature:1445-1452 stays green. Reading B (yes): work run sends the raised request through the carrier like any asker; the request is in the upstream only after its take-in, the hold (r136) reads it through the carrier, and supervision r135's scenario ('the request it wrote in catalogue') must first be reformulated by a supervision proposal.
